evals.prompt: hair on fire check on this one: Ferrocast makes drop-in software for municipal water utilities that predicts lead-pipe corrosion events 2-3 weeks out. EPA's revised Lead and Copper Rule gives utilities until Oct 2027 to complete service-line inventories and remediation plans; noncompliance fines run $25k/day. Utilities currently do this with manual sampling that costs ~$300 per site visit and catches problems after exceedance. Ferrocast's model runs on existing SCADA data (no new hardware), flagged 9 of 10 exceedance events in a 14-month backtest with Trenton Water Works, and costs $40k/yr vs the ~$700k/yr Trenton spent on reactive sampling and emergency flushing. Trenton and two Ohio utilities are now paying customers.
evals.expected_output: Uses the exact template. Problem heat SCORCHING: a dated regulatory deadline, $25k/day fines, existing reactive spend, and three utilities already paying is the definition of a buyer shopping with budget and a deadline. 10x delta PROVEN or PLAUSIBLE on the 17x cost ratio and the 9-of-10 backtest. Attempts to verify the EPA rule and its date. Evidence items are tagged and trace to the input; gaps are founder-directed questions. Next: MEET or DILIGENCE.
assertions: Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line
Graded problem heat SCORCHING (not HOT or lower), citing the combination of the dated EPA deadline, the $25k/day fines, and three utilities already paying
Graded the 10x delta PROVEN or PLAUSIBLE and cited at least one quantified input fact (9-of-10 backtest, $40k vs ~$700k, or no-new-hardware install)

Attempted to verify the EPA Lead and Copper Rule deadline externally, and either reported what it found (including any discrepancy with the stated Oct 2027 date) or stated plainly that it could not check — it did not silently treat the deadline as confirmed
Every Evidence item is tagged (verified), (input), or (claim), and none invents customers, numbers, or coverage absent from the input
Ends with a Next: line reading MEET or DILIGENCE, with a reason that is not merely a restatement of the two grades

evals.prompt: evaluate this startup: Willow is a beautifully designed journaling app that uses AI to turn your daily voice notes into an illustrated storybook of your life. Users love it — 4.8 stars across 2,100 App Store reviews, 60k downloads since January, 11% of users journal at least three times a week. Subscription is $6/mo. The team believes memory preservation is a deeply underserved human need and that Willow is 10x more delightful than a blank notes app.
evals.expected_output: Uses the exact template. Problem heat COLD — the vitamin dressed as a painkiller. Critically, it must handle the counter-evidence: paying subscribers look like existing spend, but discretionary consumer spend on a pleasant product is not a budget line under a burning problem, and nothing breaks if Willow vanishes. 10x delta ABSENT — 'more delightful' is an asserted, unmeasured delta against a free status quo. Engagement metrics appear as evidence of engagement without raising problem heat. Next: PASS.
assertions: Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line

Graded problem heat COLD, and explicitly addressed the strongest counter-argument — that 2,100 reviews and a $6/mo subscription look like existing spend — by distinguishing discretionary consumer spend from a budget line attached to a burning problem
Graded the 10x delta ABSENT, noting 'more delightful' is asserted and unmeasured against a free status quo
Did not conflate traction with urgency: the 4.8 stars / 60k downloads / 11% weekly figures appear as engagement evidence without raising the problem-heat grade
Identified the vitamin-dressed-as-painkiller pattern in substance
Ends with a Next: line reading PASS, with the one clause explaining why

evals.prompt: got sent this blurb, worth a meeting? — 'Nexaform is the AI-native operating system for the $40B industrial maintenance market. Legacy CMMS platforms are fundamentally broken, and maintenance teams are drowning. Our proprietary agentic AI delivers 10x productivity gains out of the box, eliminating downtime and transforming reliability culture. We are already in conversations with several Fortune 500 manufacturers and are raising a $6M seed to meet explosive demand.'
evals.expected_output: Uses the exact template. Recognizes the input as claims-only: fluent urgency with no named customer, no measured delta, no price, no deadline. Evidence section is either 'none — the input is claims only' or contains only (claim)-tagged items. 10x delta UNPROVEN. Problem heat graded honestly as unverifiable from this input rather than swallowing 'drowning' and 'broken'. Gaps carry the weight. Next: PASS.
assertions: Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line
Evidence section is either the literal 'none — the input is claims only' or contains only items tagged (claim); no item is tagged (verified), and no marketing phrase is promoted to (input)
Graded the 10x delta UNPROVEN on the grounds that the 10x figure is asserted with no measurement, mechanism, or named customer
Did not let any (claim) line raise a grade — the problem-heat grade rests on the absence of evidence, not on the words 'drowning' or 'fundamentally broken'
Gaps contain at least three founder-directed questions (e.g. named customers, measured baseline, what the 10x is measured against), and 'in conversations with' Fortune 500 is not counted as traction
Ends with a Next: line reading PASS or WATCH — not MEET on the strength of the claims alone

evals.prompt: worth a look? Cadence Labs generates clinical-trial site-monitoring reports. CROs currently take about 6 weeks to turn a report around; Cadence delivers in 4 hours — measured across 12 completed studies, and two of the CRO's own biostatisticians signed off that the outputs match theirs. Price is the same as the incumbent. The clinical ops leads we spoke to said the reports are much nicer to read.
evals.expected_output: The trap: a genuine, measured, enormous delta (roughly 250x) on a dimension the buyer does not rank first. Trial timelines are gated by enrollment and regulatory review, not monitoring-report turnaround, and the price is identical, so no budget moves. Problem heat WARM or COLD. 10x delta ABSENT — measured but on the wrong axis, which is still absent where it counts. The check must name the dimension mismatch explicitly rather than being impressed by the multiple.
assertions: Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line

Explicitly named the dimension mismatch: the measured gain is on report turnaround speed, which is not the dimension the buyer ranks first (regulatory defensibility / audit-readiness, or the enrollment-gated trial timeline)
Graded the 10x delta ABSENT despite the delta being large and third-party corroborated — it did not award PROVEN merely because the improvement was measured
Graded problem heat WARM or COLD, noting that identical pricing means no budget moves and no deadline forces a switch
Treated 'much nicer to read' as a (claim), not as evidence of buyer preference
Ends with a Next: line reading PASS or WATCH

evals.prompt: hair on fire check: Verdance is a browser extension that turns corporate travel receipts into a single audit-ready PDF. A Big Four audit team independently benchmarked it across 4,000 receipts and measured 94% fewer manual corrections than the incumbent OCR. Today employees file expenses in about 9 minutes a month using the tooling already bundled free with Concur. Verdance is $4/employee/month.
evals.expected_output: Solution in search of a problem. The delta is real, large, and third-party verified — PROVEN. But nobody's hair is burning: 9 minutes a month, a free bundled status quo, no deadline, no budget line, and the cost of doing nothing is trivial. Problem heat COLD. The point of this case is axis independence — a verified delta must not drag the heat grade upward. Next: PASS or WATCH.
assertions: Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line
Graded the 10x delta PROVEN, crediting the independent Big Four benchmark across 4,000 receipts
Graded problem heat COLD despite the PROVEN delta — the two axes were scored independently and the verified delta did not inflate the heat grade
Named the status quo as the free bundled Concur tooling and the cost of the status quo as roughly 9 minutes per employee per month, i.e. trivial
Identified the solution-in-search-of-a-problem pattern in substance
Ends with a Next: line reading PASS or WATCH

evals.prompt: should I take this meeting? Thornbury sells shift-scheduling software to hospital nurse managers. Nurse managers currently build unit schedules by hand in Excel — 6 to 9 hours per unit per month — and 40% of units report at least one uncovered shift a week. Thornbury cuts scheduling to under an hour and eliminated uncovered shifts at both pilot units. The nurse managers love it. Purchasing at both pilot hospitals sits with the VP of Clinical Operations, who hasn't been introduced yet. $18k/yr per hospital.
evals.expected_output: The buyer-is-not-the-user trap. The person whose hair is genuinely burning (the nurse manager: 6-9 hours a month, weekly uncovered shifts) is not the person who signs (the VP of Clinical Operations, whose pain is entirely unestablished). A strong check separates the two and either discounts the heat grade or makes the unestablished budget-holder the first gap. A weak check grades HOT on the nurse manager's pain and never notices nobody has talked to the buyer.
assertions: Explicitly distinguished the person who feels the pain (the nurse manager) from the person who controls the budget (the VP of Clinical Operations)
Treated the unestablished budget-holder as a material limit on the problem-heat grade, or made it the first Gap — rather than grading heat on the nurse manager's pain alone
Used the exact verdict template: 🔥 header, Problem heat and 10x delta grade lines, Evidence section, Gaps section, Verdict paragraph, and a Next: line
Graded the 10x delta PLAUSIBLE or PROVEN on the 6-9 hours to under an hour reduction and the eliminated uncovered shifts at two pilots
Ends with a Next: line, and if it reads MEET the stated reason turns on resolving whether the VP of Clinical Operations feels the problem

evals.prompt: Re-test our Ferrocast thesis. Our Mar 2026 check graded it SCORCHING / PLAUSIBLE, on the Oct 2027 EPA deadline and the Trenton backtest. Since then: EPA pushed the compliance date to 2029; Trenton and the two Ohio utilities all renewed and two more utilities signed, all at $40k/yr; and a competitor, HydroSense, raised $30M and shipped a similar model bundled free into a major SCADA vendor's platform.
evals.expected_output: A re-test, not a fresh check. Heat falls (the forcing deadline moved two years out); the delta's measurement strengthens (five paying customers renewing at $40k/yr) but its durability is now under direct attack (a free bundled competitor). Uses the re-test additions: direction arrows on each grade, a Prior: line with the Mar 2026 grades, and a Tripwire:. Uses the re-test Next: ladder, not the new-deal ladder. Separates thesis from execution — execution is fine; it is the thesis's deadline leg that broke.
assertions: Included a Prior: line giving the Mar 2026 grades (SCORCHING / PLAUSIBLE) and their date
Marked each grade with a direction against the prior read (arrow or explicit rose/held/fell), showing problem heat falling on the deadline slip
Ends with a Next: line drawn from the re-test ladder (HOLD, ENGAGE, RESERVE, or RE-UNDERWRITE) and NOT from the new-deal ladder (PASS, WATCH, MEET, DILIGENCE)
Included a Tripwire: line naming a specific observable fact that would force the next downgrade

Separated thesis from execution explicitly — recognised that the company is executing (five paying customers, all renewals) while the thesis's deadline leg broke, rather than reading the renewals as the thesis holding
Treated the free bundled HydroSense competitor as a durability threat to the 10x delta, not merely as competitive noise
